rule: S_N must not be null
rationale: S_N serves as the primary join key linking to Acc_Info_dirty.S_N with one-to-one cardinality. As a mandatory identifier field, it must be populated for all records.

rule: Every S_N in Cust_Bio_dirty must exist in Acc_Info_dirty.S_N
rationale: S_N is designated as a one-to-one shared key with Acc_Info_dirty. Referential integrity must be maintained to ensure all biographical records have corresponding account information.

rule: Account_No must be exactly 4 digits
rationale: Account numbers are 4-digit identifiers ranging from 1001-1028. The field should be stored as string but currently contains integer values; format validation ensures consistency.

rule: Account_No must be unique across records
rationale: Evidence indicates 2 duplicate values (1001 and 1010) appearing in multiple records. Unless business rules explicitly permit shared accounts, account numbers should be unique to prevent identification conflicts.

rule: Name must follow Title Case convention (excluding lowercase particles like bin, binte, s/o, d/o)
rationale: Sample contains case deviations: 'lim wei jie' (all lowercase) and 'WANG SHI JIE' (all uppercase). Standardization to Title Case improves consistency while preserving culturally specific lowercase particles.

check_params.logic: any((w[0].islower() if len(w) > 0 else False) or w.isupper() for w in str(row['Name']).split() if w.lower() not in ('bin','binte','d/o','s/o') and len(w) > 1)

rule: Name particles indicating gender must match the Gender column (Bin/s/o indicate Male; Binte/d/o indicate Female)
rationale: Dataset contains Malay patronymics (Bin/Binte) and Indian patronymics (s/o/d/o) that encode gender. For example, 'Danish Bin Kamaruddin' should correspond to Male, and 'Shalini d/o Krishnan' to Female. Mismatches indicate data entry errors.

check_params.logic: (bool(re.search(r'\bBin\b|\bs/o\b', str(row['Name']), re.IGNORECASE)) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'male') or (bool(re.search(r'\bBinte\b|\bd/o\b', str(row['Name']), re.IGNORECASE)) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'female')

rule: ID_No must follow Singapore NRIC/FIN format: one letter (S/T/F/G), followed by 7 digits, ending with one uppercase letter
rationale: 93.3% of values follow the standard 9-character format (e.g., S1234567A). Anomalies include '1916569C' (missing prefix) and 'F212233V' (6 digits instead of 7). This regex validates the standard format.

rule: ID_No must be unique across records
rationale: National ID numbers should uniquely identify individuals. Evidence shows one duplicate value 'F1011121T' appearing in 2 records, which requires clarification or deduplication.

rule: ID_No must match the corresponding ID value in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: Both tables contain Singapore NRIC/FIN numbers (Cust_Bio_dirty.ID_No and Acc_Info_dirty.ID) that should be consistent for the same individual identified by S_N. Sample discrepancies (e.g., S8421753J vs S8421753X) indicate synchronization errors.

check_params.semantic_check: ID_No must exactly match ID for records with the same S_N

rule: Race must be one of: Chinese, Malay, Indian
rationale: Observed values represent three semantic categories with inconsistent casing (Malay/malay/MALAY, Indian/indian). Validation enforces the canonical Title Case set after standardization.

rule: Gender must be one of: Male, Female
rationale: Field contains two categories with casing inconsistencies (male, FEMALE). Binary gender classification should be standardized to Title Case values.

rule: Age must be numeric/integer parseable
rationale: Column is typed as int64 but contains non-numeric text 'Twenty-five' (3.3% of records). This rule flags values that cannot be parsed as numbers for standardization.

rule: Age must be between 0 and 120 (inclusive)
rationale: Human age must fall within plausible biological limits. Evidence shows invalid negative value (-5) and values below 13, which are unrealistic for a service account.

rule: Age must be at least 13 for service accounts
rationale: Evidence indicates values below 13 (specifically 4 and -5) may be unrealistic for a consumer service dataset, suggesting data entry errors or child accounts that require business review.

rule: Contact_No must not be null
rationale: Contact number is a mandatory field for customer communication. Evidence shows 6.7% missing values (2 records) that require population.

rule: Contact_No must be a valid Singapore phone number (8 digits, starting with 6, 8, or 9)
rationale: Dataset contains Singapore-based customers with mixed formats (+65 prefix, 65 prefix, plain 8-digit). One value '8964359' has only 7 digits (truncated). Singapore local numbers are exactly 8 digits starting with 6 (landline), 8 or 9 (mobile).

rule: Email must contain exactly one @ symbol and no whitespace characters
rationale: Evidence identifies 4 structurally malformed emails (13.3%): 'not-an-email' and 'useremail.com' lack @, 'nabilah@@example.com' has double @, 'zx91 @example.com' contains space. Basic email format requires local-part@domain.

rule: Email must be in lowercase
rationale: Email addresses are case-insensitive in the local part per RFC standards, but standardization to lowercase prevents deduplication issues and matches canonical form.

rule: Country must be standardized to 'Singapore'
rationale: Field contains 8 variations of the same country (Singapore, SINGAPORE, singapore, S'pore, SG, Singapura, 新加坡, Republic of Singapore). All variants should be standardized to the canonical Title Case form 'Singapore'.

rule: Street_Name must not be in all uppercase
rationale: 29 of 30 values follow Title Case convention. One value 'HOLLAND ROAD' appears in all caps and should be standardized to 'Holland Road' to match the dominant format.

rule: Postal_Code must be exactly 6 digits
rationale: Singapore postal codes are strictly 6-digit numbers. Evidence shows length variations including 4-digit ('6907') and 5-digit ('99999') values that are either missing leading zeros or are data entry errors.

rule: S_N must be unique within Cust_Bio_dirty (one-to-one join key)
rationale: One-to-one key relationship detected by MinHash analysis; duplicate values break the join.

rule: Email must be unique within Cust_Bio_dirty
rationale: Column is 96.7% distinct with duplicate value(s) ['thm@example.com'] observed; treated as a candidate identifier — duplicates flagged for review.
